name: add_tests_sql_first_login_per_user
description: Write pytest-free sqlite3 assertions for a first-login-per-user window-function view; mutation-checked (ordering direction flipped so the LATEST login wins, rn=1 loosened to rn<=2, PARTITION BY dropped entirely so only one row survives across ALL users)
prompts: schema.sql (already correct - do not modify it) defines a logins table and a VIEW first_login_per_user using ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_at ASC) to surface each user's EARLIEST login record only - exactly one row per distinct user_id that appears in logins. Write a Python test file at exactly test_first_login.py that opens an in-memory sqlite3 database, loads schema.sql, seeds at least three users (including one user with MULTIPLE login rows, so the earliest-wins logic is actually exercised) with a clear earliest login per user, queries the view, and asserts on the EXACT rows returned (user_id, login_at, ip) - not just a row count. Exit non-zero (e.g. via a failed assert) on any mismatch; print something on success.

setup_files.schema.sql:
CREATE TABLE logins (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  login_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  ip TEXT NOT NULL
);

-- Each user's EARLIEST login record only (ties broken arbitrarily by
-- sqlite - the fixtures below never have exact ties).
CREATE VIEW first_login_per_user AS
SELECT user_id, login_at, ip FROM (
  SELECT user_id, login_at, ip,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_at ASC) AS rn
  FROM logins
) ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY user_id;

test_setup_files.mutation_check.py:
"""Mutation harness: model tests must PASS against the real schema.sql and
FAIL against each mutant. Uses a Python-level subprocess timeout (not a
shell `timeout` wrapper)."""
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

IMPL = Path("schema.sql")
TEST = "test_first_login.py"
MUTANTS = [
    # keeps the LATEST login per user instead of the earliest
    ["ORDER BY login_at ASC", "ORDER BY login_at DESC"],
    # keeps the two earliest logins per user instead of just one
    ["WHERE rn = 1", "WHERE rn <= 2"],
    # PARTITION BY dropped entirely - row numbers are assigned globally, so
    # only ONE row survives across ALL users combined, not one per user
    ["ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_at ASC)",
     "ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY login_at ASC)"],
]


def run_tests() -> int:
    for p in Path(".").rglob("__pycache__"):
        shutil.rmtree(p, ignore_errors=True)
    try:
        return subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-B", TEST], timeout=30).returncode
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return 124


src = IMPL.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
for old, _new in MUTANTS:
    assert src.count(old) == 1, (
        f"protected implementation file {IMPL} was modified - the task said not to "
        f"change it (anchor not found exactly once: {old!r})")

rc = run_tests()
assert rc == 0, f"model tests FAILED against the correct schema (exit {rc})"

try:
    for i, (old, new) in enumerate(MUTANTS, 1):
        IMPL.write_text(src.replace(old, new), encoding="utf-8")
        rc = run_tests()
        assert rc != 0, (
            f"mutation {i} SURVIVED: the tests still pass against a deliberately "
            f"broken view definition, so they do not verify the required behavior")
finally:
    IMPL.write_text(src, encoding="utf-8")

print(f"PASS (killed all {len(MUTANTS)} mutants)")

reference_solution.test_first_login.py:
import sqlite3

con = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
con.executescript(open("schema.sql", encoding="utf-8").read())

con.executescript("""
INSERT INTO logins (user_id, login_at, ip) VALUES
  (1, '2026-01-01T09:00:00', '10.0.0.1'),
  (1, '2026-01-03T09:00:00', '10.0.0.2'),
  (1, '2026-01-02T09:00:00', '10.0.0.3'),
  (2, '2026-02-05T14:00:00', '10.0.0.9'),
  (3, '2026-03-01T08:00:00', '10.0.0.5'),
  (3, '2026-03-02T08:00:00', '10.0.0.6');
""")

rows = con.execute(
    "SELECT user_id, login_at, ip FROM first_login_per_user"
).fetchall()

assert rows == [
    (1, '2026-01-01T09:00:00', '10.0.0.1'),
    (2, '2026-02-05T14:00:00', '10.0.0.9'),
    (3, '2026-03-01T08:00:00', '10.0.0.5'),
], f"unexpected rows: {rows}"

# exactly one row per user - the view must not leak extra rows
user_ids = [r[0] for r in rows]
assert user_ids == sorted(set(user_ids)), f"expected exactly one row per user: {rows}"
assert len(rows) == 3, f"expected 3 rows (one per user), got {len(rows)}: {rows}"

print("PASS")
